items.title: Define ledger record TypeScript types + schema validator
items.context: In a new module under packages/main/src (e.g. core/usage-ledger/record.ts), define the JSONL record type and a validator matching the spec's 'JSON Ledger Record Shape' + 'Required record constraints': four-field usage (inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens; NO totalTokens), usage.source enum (provider-reported|prompt-size-estimate|unavailable), correlation (ledgerCallId, attemptId, sequence:int, supersedesRecordIds:string[]), recordId, schemaVersion, recordedAt, projectRootHash, storyId(nullable)/phase/agentType/optional subagentId/threadId, privacy flags, authority {mode, receiptId:null, receiptVerified:false}, integrity {previousRecordHash, recordHash}. Validator rejects stored totalTokens and encodes per-dimension cache absence as null (never 0). Unit-tested for valid + each rejection.

happy.desc: Construct a valid record with all required fields (schemaVersion=1, recordId, ledgerCallId, attemptId, sequence=1, supersedesRecordIds=[], recordedAt ISO, projectRootHash, storyId, phase, agentType, usage.source=provider-reported, four token fields as integers, usage.canonical, usage.raw, privacy flags, authority{mode:local,receiptId:null,receiptVerified:false}, integrity{previousRecordHash,recordHash}) -> validator returns success with no errors; WHY: proves the golden-path record shape is accepted
Construct a valid record with usage.source=unavailable, unavailableReason set, all four token fields null -> validator accepts; WHY: covers the unavailable source variant
Construct a valid record with usage.source=prompt-size-estimate, estimator{name,version,unit,confidence} set -> validator accepts; WHY: covers estimate source variant

Construct valid provider-reported record where provider does not report cache dims -> cacheCreationInputTokens=null, cacheReadInputTokens=null, validator accepts; WHY: per-dimension absence encoded as null not 0

edge.desc: Record with totalTokens field present -> validator rejects with error mentioning totalTokens; WHY: spec forbids stored totalTokens
Record with cacheCreationInputTokens=0 when provider genuinely reports 0 -> validator accepts; WHY: 0 is valid when provider reports it, not when masking absence
Record missing required field recordId -> validator rejects; WHY: all required fields must be present
Record with usage.source not in enum (e.g. guessed) -> validator rejects; WHY: source enum is closed
Record with sequence=0 or negative -> validator rejects; WHY: sequence must be positive integer
Record with supersedesRecordIds omitted entirely -> validator rejects; WHY: field required even when empty array

adversarial.desc: Record with totalTokens nested inside usage AND at top level simultaneously -> validator rejects both locations; WHY: attacker sneaks totalTokens at multiple nesting levels
Record with inputTokens as string 100 instead of number -> validator rejects; WHY: type coercion attack on numeric fields
Record with cacheReadInputTokens=undefined (JS undefined not JSON null) -> validator rejects or treats as missing not silently 0; WHY: undefined-vs-null confusion attack

items.title: Append-only writer to .lattice/usage/llm-usage.jsonl with hash chain
items.context: Add an append-only writer (e.g. core/usage-ledger/writer.ts): ensures .lattice/usage/ exists, validates each record, computes recordHash and chains previousRecordHash from the prior line, appends exactly one JSON line. Never rewrites/edits prior lines. Reads the last record's hash to chain. No-op when the opt-in flag (CHK-006) is off.

happy.desc: Append 3 records via the writer to a temp dir -> file contains exactly 3 JSON lines, each parseable, each line recordHash matches SHA-256 of its content minus the recordHash field; WHY: proves one-line-per-record append semantics

Append 3 records -> record[0].previousRecordHash is null/empty, record[1].previousRecordHash === record[0].recordHash, record[2].previousRecordHash === record[1].recordHash; WHY: proves hash-chain continuity across 3+ records
Writer creates .lattice/usage/ directory if it does not exist -> directory created, file written; WHY: first-run path creation

edge.desc: Append a record, then read file, tamper with middle line (change a token count), recompute nothing -> next chain verification fails because record[2].previousRecordHash no longer matches tampered record[1].recordHash; WHY: proves hash-chain detects tampering
Append to an existing file with prior records -> writer reads last line hash and chains from it, does not overwrite prior lines; WHY: append-only guarantee
Writer receives an invalid record (missing required field) -> writer throws/rejects, no line appended to file; WHY: validation gate before write
Append to a file whose last line is corrupt JSON -> writer throws or refuses to chain; WHY: cannot chain from unparseable predecessor

adversarial.desc: Two concurrent appends racing on the same file -> both records appear in the file with correct hash chain (no lost writes, no corrupted lines); WHY: concurrent write safety
Record with integrity.recordHash pre-filled by caller to a wrong value -> writer overwrites it with the correct computed hash (caller cannot forge the hash); WHY: prevents hash injection

Attempt to call fs.appendFile or fs.writeFile on the ledger path from outside the writer module -> only the writer module exports the append function, no other code path can write the file; WHY: single write choke-point guarantee

items.title: Correlation-id generation helpers (minted before dispatch)
items.context: Provide helpers to mint ledgerCallId and attemptId locally BEFORE any provider request, a monotonic sequence within ledgerCallId+attemptId, and supersedesRecordIds wiring. Must NOT derive ids from provider.requestIdHash. Covered by a test asserting a preflight record and a later record for the same attempt share ledgerCallId+attemptId with increasing sequence, and that a final record can supersede an earlier one.

happy.desc: Call mintLedgerCallId() -> returns a string starting with a recognizable prefix (e.g. llmcall_), is unique across 100 calls; WHY: proves id is minted locally with stable prefix
Call mintAttemptId() -> returns a string starting with a recognizable prefix (e.g. llmatt_), is unique across 100 calls; WHY: proves attempt id minted locally

Create a preflight record (sequence=1) and a postflight record (sequence=2) for the same ledgerCallId+attemptId -> both share ledgerCallId and attemptId, sequence is monotonically increasing; WHY: correlation stability across an attempts records
Create a final record with supersedesRecordIds=[preflight-record-id] -> supersedesRecordIds contains exactly the preflight recordId; WHY: proves supersedes wiring works

edge.desc: Mint ledgerCallId when no provider request exists yet (before dispatch) -> id is returned without any provider.requestIdHash input; WHY: ids must be pre-dispatch, not derived from provider
Same ledgerCallId with two different attemptIds (retry scenario) -> both attemptIds are distinct, ledgerCallId is shared; WHY: retries reuse call id but get new attempt id
Sequence counter resets for a new attemptId under the same ledgerCallId -> sequences start from 1 again for the new attempt; WHY: sequence is per-attempt monotonic

adversarial.desc: Pass a provider.requestIdHash value to mintLedgerCallId -> function ignores it or does not accept it as a parameter (id is never derived from provider hash); WHY: prevents provider-hash-derived ids
Call mintLedgerCallId concurrently from 50 parallel calls -> all 50 ids are unique (no collision under concurrency); WHY: uniqueness under concurrent minting
Attempt to set sequence to a non-monotonic value (e.g. sequence 3 after sequence 5 for same call+attempt) -> rejected or automatically corrected; WHY: monotonicity enforcement

items.title: Runtime rejection of raw prompt/transcript/secret material
items.context: The writer/validator must reject (throw or refuse to write) any record carrying raw prompt, raw completion, raw transcript, raw tool arguments, provider secrets, customer API keys, actor keys, or authorization headers — per the spec's Privacy Constraints. Allowed: hashes, model/provider names, usage counts, reason codes, redaction profile id. Tested with an injection attempt that must be rejected.

happy.desc: Record with only allowed fields (hashes, model name, provider name, usage counts, reason codes, redaction profile id, budget policy id) -> validator/writer accepts; WHY: proves legitimate privacy-preserving fields pass

edge.desc: Record containing a field named rawPrompt with a prompt string -> writer rejects with privacy error; WHY: raw prompt is forbidden
Record containing a field named rawCompletion -> writer rejects; WHY: raw completion is forbidden
Record containing a field named rawTranscript -> writer rejects; WHY: raw transcript is forbidden
Record containing a field named toolArguments with raw tool args -> writer rejects; WHY: raw tool arguments forbidden
Record containing a field named apiKey with a real key -> writer rejects; WHY: customer API keys forbidden
Record containing a field named authorizationHeader -> writer rejects; WHY: auth headers forbidden

adversarial.desc: Record with secret material hidden inside a deeply nested extra object (e.g. metadata.debug.rawPrompt) -> writer rejects even at arbitrary nesting depth; WHY: attacker hides forbidden content in deep nesting
Record with provider secret in a field named providerSecret or providerApiKey -> writer rejects; WHY: provider secrets forbidden regardless of field naming
Record with actorKey field containing key material -> writer rejects; WHY: actor keys explicitly forbidden by spec

Record with allowed hash field (e.g. provider.requestIdHash=sha256:abc) alongside a forbidden rawPrompt field -> writer rejects the whole record (not partial acceptance); WHY: one forbidden field poisons the entire record

items.title: Register the ledger path in runtime-artifact-registry.ts
items.context: Add an entry to packages/main/src/core/runtime-artifact-registry.ts for .lattice/usage/llm-usage.jsonl: id=llm-usage-ledger, matchers (exact path or prefix .lattice/usage/), ignorePatterns .lattice/usage/, materialHash=exclude, volatile=true, repairableTrackedArtifact=true, description = local LLM usage diagnostic ledger. Ensure gitignore/doctor/material-hash tooling treat it as a mutable runtime diagnostic. Tested: the path classifies as gitignored + materialHash-exclude + volatile + repairable.

happy.desc: Call findRuntimeArtifactEntry(".lattice/usage/llm-usage.jsonl") -> returns entry with id=llm-usage-ledger; WHY: proves the ledger path is registered and findable
Call isMaterialExcludedRuntimeArtifactPath(".lattice/usage/llm-usage.jsonl") -> returns true; WHY: ledger must be excluded from material hash
Call isVolatileRuntimeArtifactPath(".lattice/usage/llm-usage.jsonl") -> returns true; WHY: ledger is volatile runtime state
Call isRepairableTrackedRuntimeArtifactPath(".lattice/usage/llm-usage.jsonl") -> returns true; WHY: ledger is repairable

edge.desc: Call findRuntimeArtifactEntry(".lattice/usage/") with prefix matcher -> returns the llm-usage-ledger entry (or a parent entry covering the prefix); WHY: prefix .lattice/usage/ should match
listRuntimeArtifactIgnorePatterns() includes .lattice/usage/ -> gitignore will cover the ledger directory; WHY: ledger path must be gitignored
Call findRuntimeArtifactEntry with a path like .lattice/usage/other-file.jsonl -> still matches the prefix matcher; WHY: future adjacent usage-runtime files are also covered

adversarial.desc: Call findRuntimeArtifactEntry with a path outside .lattice/usage/ (e.g. .lattice/story/actives/B-253e/usage.jsonl) -> does NOT match the llm-usage-ledger entry; WHY: matcher must not be overly broad and catch story evidence paths

Verify the entry has volatile=true AND repairableTrackedArtifact=true AND materialHash=exclude simultaneously -> all three properties confirmed on the same entry; WHY: a partial registration (e.g. volatile but not repairable) would be a spec violation

items.title: Opt-in flag gating + informational summary reader
items.context: Gate the writer behind an opt-in flag (env var or config, default OFF) so it is fully inert by default (Rollout Phase 2). Add a summary reader that parses the JSONL and reports totals derived as total=inputTokens+outputTokens+cacheCreationInputTokens+cacheReadInputTokens, selects the latest non-superseded accounting record per ledgerCallId+attemptId, keeps estimates out of provider-reported totals, and reports unavailable/null as unknown (never zero). Summary is informational only — it must NOT feed any gate. Tested: flag OFF => writer no-ops; summary never double-counts superseded estimates and never treats unknown as 0.

happy.desc: Opt-in flag OFF (default) -> call writer.append(validRecord) -> no file created at .lattice/usage/llm-usage.jsonl, function returns without error (strict no-op); WHY: default-off means zero side effects
Opt-in flag ON -> call writer.append(validRecord) -> file created with one line; WHY: flag gates the writer

Summary reader with 3 non-superseded provider-reported records (inputTokens=100,200,300; outputTokens=10,20,30; cacheCreation=5,10,15; cacheRead=2,4,6) -> derived totals: total per record = input+output+cacheCreation+cacheRead, aggregate = sum of per-record totals; WHY: proves derived-total identity

Summary reader with a superseded estimate and a final provider-reported record for the same ledgerCallId+attemptId -> summary selects only the final (latest non-superseded) record, does not double-count the estimate; WHY: no double-counting

edge.desc: Summary reader with a record where usage.source=unavailable and all token fields are null -> summary reports that call as unknown, not as 0; WHY: unavailable/null must never be treated as 0

Summary reader with a provider-reported record where cacheCreationInputTokens=null (per-dimension absence) -> total derivation skips null fields or reports partial unknown, never substitutes 0; WHY: null dimension must not silently become 0 in totals
Summary with two records for same ledgerCallId+attemptId where neither supersedes the other -> summary selects the one with highest sequence; WHY: latest-sequence selection rule

Summary with estimates kept separate from provider-reported totals -> estimate subtotal does not merge into provider-reported subtotal; WHY: spec requires keeping estimates out of provider-reported totals

adversarial.desc: Opt-in flag OFF -> call writer.append 10 times -> no file ever created, no directory created; WHY: no leakage even under repeated calls

Summary feeds a gate or returns a gate-consumable structure -> must not; verify the summary return type has no gate field and the function signature/docs say informational-only; WHY: summary must NOT feed any gate

Summary with a mix of provider-reported, estimate, and unavailable records for the same call across 3 attempts -> only latest non-superseded per attempt is counted, unavailable attempts reported as unknown not 0, estimates never merged into provider totals; WHY: complex multi-attempt multi-source scenario

items.title: Smoke/test suite wired into package.json
items.context: Add a smoke test (packages/main/src/tasks/usage-ledger-smoke.ts, wired as an npm test script) covering: schema validation (valid + each rejection incl. stored totalTokens and raw-content), append + hash-chain continuity across multiple records, correlation-id stability + supersedes, opt-in flag OFF => no file written, runtime-artifact classification of the ledger path, and summary correctness (derived totals, no double-count, unknown!=0). Build green; run via npm.

happy.desc: npm --prefix packages/main run build -> exits 0 with no TypeScript errors; WHY: build must be green with all new code
npm --prefix packages/main run test:usage-ledger (or equivalent wired script name) -> exits 0, runs all smoke assertions; WHY: smoke is wired as an npm script and passes
packages/main/package.json contains a script entry whose name matches test:usage-ledger or test:llm-usage-ledger -> script exists and points to the smoke file; WHY: proves npm wiring

edge.desc: Smoke covers schema validation: valid record accepted, stored totalTokens rejected, raw-content injection rejected, malformed record rejected -> all sub-assertions pass; WHY: integration coverage of CHK-001 + CHK-004
Smoke covers append + hash-chain continuity across >=3 records -> chain verified programmatically; WHY: integration coverage of CHK-002
Smoke covers correlation-id stability + supersedes wiring -> preflight and postflight share ids, supersedes works; WHY: integration coverage of CHK-003
Smoke covers opt-in flag OFF -> no file written; WHY: integration coverage of CHK-006 gating
Smoke covers runtime-artifact classification of .lattice/usage/llm-usage.jsonl -> gitignored + materialHash-exclude + volatile + repairable; WHY: integration coverage of CHK-005
Smoke covers summary correctness: derived totals match identity, no double-count of superseded, unknown != 0; WHY: integration coverage of CHK-006 summary

adversarial.desc: Run the smoke in a clean temp directory with no prior .lattice/usage/ -> smoke creates and cleans up its own test artifacts, does not pollute the repo; WHY: test isolation
Run npm --prefix packages/main run build && npm --prefix packages/main run test:usage-ledger in sequence -> both pass end-to-end; WHY: full CI pipeline simulation
